dedupe_keys.name: mms assessment update of offshore oil and gas infrastructure damage from hurricanes katrina and rita press release 3486 1 may 2006

description: This case study is a US Minerals Management Service press release, number 3486 of 1 May 2006, updating its assessment of damage to offshore oil and gas infrastructure caused by Hurricanes Katrina and Rita in 2005. It reports that the number of damaged pipelines had risen from 183 to 457, that 101 of them were 10 inches or larger and 32 were back in service, that destroyed platforms were revised from 115 to 113, and that four replacement platforms were approved to take the place of eight destroyed ones producing 16,700 barrels per day. It adds a tally of 146 spills of at least one barrel in federal waters and attached tables list the major damaged pipelines and destroyed platforms. Access: free PDF at the BOEM newsroom archive; no licence is stated. Coverage is the Gulf of Mexico Outer Continental Shelf. Caveats: the figures are interim, the agency itself expected more damage to be reported, and only this release was read here. It suits hazard exposure and resilience studies of offshore energy assets, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

name: MMS assessment update of offshore oil and gas infrastructure damage from Hurricanes Katrina and Rita (press release 3486, 1 May 2006)
organisations: Minerals Management Service (US Department of the Interior)
outcomes: The updated count of damaged offshore pipelines rose to 457 from 183, of which 101 were 10 inches or larger (up from 64) and 32 had returned to service; 113 platforms were listed as destroyed (revised down from 115), with four replacement platforms approved for eight destroyed platforms that had produced 16,700 barrels per day. The release also tallies 146 spills of 1 barrel or more, six of 1,000 barrels or more, the largest 3,625 barrels of condensate, and warns further damage was likely as underwater surveys were delayed by scarce diving and vessel support.
